messages:
sam: Heads up — I just flagged a weird spike: deploy-proxy serviceAccount performed KMS decrypts in prod (~30 decrypt events in the last hour) outside any rollout windows. audit logs attached. :eyes:

elaine: paste the audit snippet? is that the SA our pipeline uses for canaries?

mike: this smells like the old clusterrolebinding we inherited from the mono-repo days. grep for deploy-proxy-binding and we might find a wide ClusterRole.

security-bot: ALERT: anomalous_kms_usage - serviceAccount:infra/deploy-proxy@redwood-prod performed decrypt on key 'redwood-prod-enc' (30 events). Investigate immediate.

sam: snippets:
```
# audit log excerpt
{"protoPayload": {"methodName":"google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt","serviceName":"cloudkms.googleapis.com","authenticationInfo":{"principalEmail":"deploy-proxy@infra.svc.cluster.local"},"resourceName":"projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/main/cryptoKeys/redwood-prod-enc"}, "timestamp":"2026-03-20T12:04:01Z"}
```

and kubectl check I ran: ```kubectl get clusterrolebinding deploy-proxy-binding -o yaml``` returned a binding to cluster-admin (yep).

elaine: cluster-admin? ugh. that's why. quick mitigation: can we remove the binding and add a scoped RoleBinding that only allows sign/encrypt but not decrypt? also consider a short deny in the KMS IAM for that SA while we triage.

mike: agree. Plan: 1) remove ClusterRoleBinding 2) create a namespaced Role with explicit verbs (get/list/watch) for configmaps/secrets used by deploy, but no KMS permissions. 3) Create a separate service account with minimal KMS decrypt if required by a specific job (and require impersonation for that job).

sam: command I ran to find the binding:
```
kubectl get clusterrolebinding deploy-proxy-binding -o yaml
# snippet
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: deploy-proxy
  namespace: infra
roleRef:
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
  kind: ClusterRole
  name: cluster-admin
```

auditor-bot: NOTE: policy drift detected. Resource deploy-proxy-binding was created 2023-06-11 by ops-admin. Historical justification missing.

elaine: immediate steps: (A) remove binding (kubectl delete clusterrolebinding deploy-proxy-binding) behind a canary change window, (B) add a temporary KMS IAM Deny for that SA on key 'redwood-prod-enc' (deny policy in org level) to stop further decrypts, (C) schedule a short postmortem and RBAC refactor ticket. anyone object to those being immediate? :lock:

mike: no objections. note: deleting the binding will likely break some scheduled rollout job that unexpectedly used cluster-admin. We'll try a canary: disable at 12:30 UTC for one cluster, watch deploy-monitor.

sam: I can monitor audit logs and key usage during the canary. also recommend rotating the key if we confirm unauthorized usage — defensively.

elaine: created ticket: ISSUE-2342 (RBAC: remove cluster-admin from deploy-proxy + KMS deny + scoped role + key rotation). assigning to @mike and @elaine. ETA for mitigation window: 2 hours.

mike: will prepare RBAC patch. proposed Role (namespaced):
```
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: deploy-runner
  namespace: infra
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["pods","pods/exec","configmaps"]
  verbs: ["get","list","create","patch"]
```

sam: also let's add an admission webhook check to block future ClusterRoleBindings referencing deploy-proxy unless a ticket id is present in annotation. small guardrail.

elaine: agree. I'll own the webhook RFC. for now: add KMS deny and schedule canary. mike & sam — sync 5m before delete.

deploy-bot: deploy pipeline triggered: canary/rbac-mitigation -> infra (holding for manual approval).

sam: thanks — monitoring. will post updates in this thread and escalate to incident if more decrypts show up. :white_check_mark:

auditor-bot: ACTION: attach audit record to ISSUE-2342 and mark this event as "investigate-rbac-leak".

elaine: follow-ups: create a short playbook entry for KMS anomalous decrypts (who to notify, short-term denies, key-rotation checklist). I'll add it to runbook repo.

mike: after mitigation, propose a small refactor: split deploy service accounts by role (canary-runner, release-manager), require IAM roles for KMS only via GCP IAM and not via cluster-level RBAC. reduces blast radius.

sam: sounds good. logging: keep these audit logs for 90 days; correlate with CI triggers to see if this was a pipeline step misuse or leaked creds.

elaine: thanks team. report back after canary. :coffee:
